data: My family’s fished this lake for years, and I want it to keep supporting our village. How about we each catch 10 tons this month? That gives each of us $10,000 and leaves 50 tons, which doubles back to 100 for next month. If we stick to that, we can keep earning without draining the lake. Once catches are revealed, let’s review them together and agree on next month’s limits. John, would you agree to 10 tons each?

I’m in for 10 tons, Luke. My family taught me to leave enough fish for the next catch, and this plan protects everyone’s livelihood. If someone needs extra one month, let’s discuss it beforehand and agree on an offset so our combined catch stays at 50 tons or less. John, can you commit to 10 tons too?

I’ll commit to 10 tons too. My family depends on this lake, and I want our village to have that same livelihood for years to come. Let’s make 10 tons each our standing agreement, then check the lake’s stock and everyone’s catches each month before renewing it. Jack, are you willing to join us?

Count me in for 10 tons. That’s a steady income without taking away next month’s livelihood. If the lake starts a future month below 100 tons, let’s lower our combined catch to leave at least half the stock to reproduce. Jack, will you join the agreement?

I’m in—I’ll catch 10 tons this month. My family taught me that a good catch should leave a future for the village, too. That makes all five of us agreed. Let’s check the revealed catches and lake stock together before setting next month’s limits.
